texts.preamble: State Of Maharashtra vs Watan S/O Bhayyaji Kokas & 5 Others on 26 February, 2018 Author: V. M. Deshpande Bench: V. M. Deshpande 1 APPEAL214.02.odt In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay : Nagpur Bench : Nagpur. Criminal Appeal No. 214 Of 2002 Appellant : State of Maharashtra, through Mr. Jagdish Khushal Kamble, Food Inspector, Food and Drug Administration(M.S.), Chandrapur, Tah. And Dist. Chandrapur. Versus
texts.facts: The facts giving rise to the present appeal, in short, are as under : The complainant Jagdish Khushal Kamble, (PW1) was appointed as a Food Inspector in the year 1972. When he was discharging his duties as Food Inspector at Chandrapur, on 21.1.1999, he along with Naresh Bhagwat Goswami (PW4) visited the premises of M/s Suhas Food Products situated at E-79, M.I.D.C., Chandrapur, respondent no.1 was present in the factory. The complainant Shri Kamble (PW1) disclosed his identity to him and shown his inclination to draw samples of food articles for the purpose of testing and analysis. He inspected the premises and drawn Inspection Report (Exh.22). During the inspection, he found 100 packed identical packets of pasteurized and homogenized cow milk and pasteurized and homogenized double tonned milk. Each packet was of one liter. He selected one packet of both milk for the purpose of sample. He demanded 750 ml each quality of milk from the State Of Maharashtra vs Watan S/O Bhayyaji Kokas & 5 Others on 26 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141175911/ 2 respondent no.1. Accordingly, the said was given to the complainant in two different clean, dry and empty containers. He paid the cost of the samples and obtained receipt from the respondent no.1 (Exh.23). He also prepared the notice as 4 APPEAL214.02.odt contemplated under Section 14-A of the Act of 1954 and handed over the same to the respondent no.1. He thereafter divided the samples equally in three clean, dry and empty bottles and also added 20 drops of Formalin as preservative in each sample bottle. Those were sealed by him. He, thereafter sent the packet to the Public Analyst, Public Health Laboratory, Nagpur. He also gave an intimation as required under the Act of 1954 through the Legal Health Authority. The report of the Public Analyst dated 03.3.1999 (Exh.39) was received and as per the report, the sample was not in conformity with the standard as per the Rules framed under the Act of 1954. 4. As per the prosecution case, thereafter, the Local Health Authority and Assistant Commissioner for Food and Drug Administration, forwarded his proposal with all relevant documents to the Joint Commissioner of Food and Drug Administration at Nagpur on 29.4.1999 (Exh.45). After obtaining consent, the complaint was lodged in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chandrapur. 5 APPEAL214.02.odt 5. The learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chandrapur framed the Charge against the respondents in Regular Criminal Case No. 326 of 1999 under Exh.52. In order to bring home the guilt of the respondents, the complainant examined in all four witnesses. They are (1) Jagdish Khushal Kamble (P.W.1), the complainant. ; (2) Ashok Purushottam Choudhary, Assistant Commissioner, F.D.A., Chandrapur, who received the proposal from the Food Inspector (PW1) and as per his claim, gave a letter dated 08.7.1999 to the respondents for exercising their right under Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954 ; (3) Prakash Narayan Shende, Drug Inspector, Yavatmal ; and (4) Naresh Bhagwat Goswami, a panch witness, in whose presence PW1 obtained samples from the respondent no.1. 6.
texts.arguments: 6 APPEAL214.02.odt Sub-section 2 of Section 13 of the Act, reads as under : "13. Report of Public Analyst :- (1) ...... (2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other State Of Maharashtra vs Watan S/O Bhayyaji Kokas & 5 Others on 26 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141175911/ 3 particulars have been disclosed under section 14-A forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the Court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory." 8. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Municipal Council, Delhi .vs. Ghisa Ram [AIR 1967 SC 970] has ruled that a right conferred by Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954 to the accused is indefeasible and valuable right since the Certificate of the Director of Central Laboratory supersedes the report of the Public Analyst and has to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents.
